Prongs point at the lower-left side of the strip below the two outlet faces. Source defines no receiving socket at that location; both views show exposed prongs meeting the shell. This is distinguished from head contact.

The model aims its independently placed plug at the strip's lower-left corner and says the prongs penetrate there. Only the two empty outlet plates are constructed; no receiving socket is provided at the contact. Source and both views agree.

interpretation: This particular general checking instruction produced no seated receiving socket in either of its two calls; the two fresh baselines had the same category counts.
This is not evidence that checking prompts never help, nor an estimate of a treatment effect. The cohort is too small, and a different general instruction or rendered feedback could differ.
The two strip-contact cases show why a binary head-versus-strip label is insufficient for fidelity: moving prongs to a shell is different from depicting a receiving socket.

Source inspection shows positive surface objects used as outlet marks in this cohort. Functional negative-volume geometry was added as a separate investigation after the fidelity protocol was committed; it is not retroactively treated as a preregistered endpoint of this round.
The model's uncertainty and interpretation statements remain properties of the responses, not independent proof of insufficient grounding in the source.
